description: Statutes and rules that interact with Civil Code § 3294 punitive damages in California civil practice.

refs.relationship: § 1572 fraud elements directly satisfy § 3294(c)(3) fraud definition. Every § 1572 claim supports a § 3294 prayer.
Tort deceit independent of contract. § 3294 punitives are routinely paired with § 1709 claims.

§ 3295(c) restricts pre-trial discovery of defendant's financial condition unless the court finds substantial probability plaintiff will prevail on the punitive claim. This is the procedural gate that must be opened before a forensic accountant can develop the financial-condition evidence that Adams v. Murakami requires.

refs.target: California Code of Civil Procedure § 377.34 (damages in survival actions)
refs.relationship: § 377.34 bars punitive damages in survival actions generally; § 3294(d) carves out a narrow exception for homicide-based wrongful death with felony conviction.

refs.target: California Civil Code § 3343 (real property fraud out-of-pocket damages)
refs.relationship: § 3343 provides the compensatory baseline for real property fraud; the § 3294 punitive award is calculated as a ratio to the § 3343 compensatory award under the BMW/State Farm framework.

refs.target: BMW of North America, Inc. v. Gore (1996) 517 U.S. 559
refs.relationship: Federal due process three-guidepost analysis: reprehensibility, ratio, comparison to civil penalties. Binding on California courts as federal constitutional law.

refs.target: State Farm Mutual Auto Ins. Co. v. Campbell (2003) 538 U.S. 408
refs.relationship: Federal due process ratio presumption: single-digit ratios are presumptively constitutional; ratios above 9:1 require extraordinary reprehensibility.

refs.target: Simon v. San Paolo U.S. Holding Co. (2005) 35 Cal.4th 1159
refs.relationship: California Supreme Court's synthesis of the Gore/State Farm guideposts for use by California trial and appellate courts.

Judicial Council Civil Jury Instructions on punitive damages. CACI 3940 articulates the despicable-conduct threshold from College Hospital. CACI 3942 addresses the managing-agent rule from White v. Ultramar. CACI 3945 addresses the clear-and-convincing burden of proof.
